lit: to wipe one's eyes clean and wait (so as to see clearly what happens)

use.how: Usually ends the sentence and rarely takes an object: 让我们拭目以待。 Said of an outcome people are curious or doubtful about.

near.diff: 翘首以待 is eager longing for something hoped for; 拭目以待 is watching to see how an uncertain thing turns out, often with some doubt.

cue: A rival company boasts its new phone will beat everyone. You doubt it, but the launch will show. What do you say?

ctx.s: 新电影下个月上映，到底好不好看，我们{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: The new film comes out next month; whether it's any good, we'll see.

ctx.s: 他说今年一定能考上研究生，大家都在{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: He says he will definitely get into graduate school this year, and everyone is waiting to see.

ctx.s: “这家新餐厅能撑过一年吗？”“不好说，{拭目以待}吧。”
ctx.en: "Will this new restaurant last a year?" "Hard to say. Let's wait and see."

ctx.s: 新市长承诺解决交通问题，市民们正{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: The new mayor has promised to fix the traffic problem, and residents are waiting to see if he delivers.

ctx.s: 这项技术能否真正改变我们的生活，还需要{拭目以待}。
ctx.en: Whether this technology will really change our lives remains to be seen.

ctx.s: 两支球队实力相当，决赛谁能夺冠，让我们{拭目以待}！
ctx.en: The two teams are evenly matched; who will win the final? Let's wait and see!

bad.s: 我饿坏了，正在门口{拭目以待}外卖。
bad.en: (meant: I'm starving and waiting at the door for my takeaway)
bad.why: It is about watching how a notable, uncertain outcome turns out, not waiting for something ordinary, and it normally takes no object.

bad.s: 听到这个坏消息，她伤心得{拭目以待}。
bad.en: (meant: she was so sad she wiped away tears)
bad.why: The eye-wiping here is clearing the eyes to watch closely, not wiping away tears; the idiom has nothing to do with crying.

mean: the one who spoils it for the whole group
lit: the horse that harms the herd

story.text: The Yellow Emperor lost his way and met a boy herding horses who knew the road. Impressed, the emperor asked him how to govern the world. The boy said it was no different from herding horses: simply get rid of whatever harms the herd.

use.how: A noun, usually after 是 or 成了: 他是我们班的害群之马。 Names one member whose behaviour damages the whole group's work or name.

cue: One player keeps breaking team rules, and now the whole squad is punished with extra training. What is he to the team?

ctx.s: 全班同学都很守纪律，只有他是{害群之马}。
ctx.en: The whole class follows the rules; he is the only bad apple.

ctx.s: 一个员工收了回扣，公司马上开除了这个{害群之马}。
ctx.en: One employee took kickbacks, and the company fired the bad apple at once.

ctx.s: 少数无良商家是这个行业的{害群之马}，让顾客失去了信任。
ctx.en: A few dishonest sellers are the black sheep of the trade and have cost it customers' trust.

ctx.s: “为什么大家都被罚？”“还不是因为那个{害群之马}！”
ctx.en: "Why is everyone being punished?" "Because of that one troublemaker, of course!"

ctx.s: 教练说，球队不需要明星，更不需要{害群之马}。
ctx.en: The coach said the team doesn't need stars, and it needs troublemakers even less.

ctx.s: 他总在背后挑拨同事关系，成了部门里的{害群之马}。
ctx.en: He kept stirring up trouble between colleagues behind their backs and became the bad apple of the department.

bad.s: 他是我们队的{害群之马}，每场比赛都进球。
bad.en: (meant: he's our team's star, scoring in every match)
bad.why: It is harsh criticism of someone who harms the group; it can never be praise for a standout member.

bad.s: 这家公司的员工全都是{害群之马}。
bad.en: (meant: every employee of this company is bad)
bad.why: It singles out one or a few who spoil a group; if everyone is bad there is no herd for them to harm.

mean: made even stronger by a new advantage
lit: like a tiger that grows wings

use.how: A predicate, often 真是如虎添翼 or 让……如虎添翼. Said when someone already strong gains a new advantage that makes them stronger still.

near.diff: 锦上添花 adds a pleasant extra to something already good; 如虎添翼 adds strength, making someone already powerful more formidable.

cue: Your debate team, already the champions, has just recruited the best speaker from a rival school. How do you describe the team now?

ctx.s: 球队本来就很强，又来了一位明星前锋，真是{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: The team was already strong, and now a star striker has joined; it's like giving a tiger wings.

ctx.s: 她英语已经很好，再学会西班牙语，找工作就{如虎添翼}了。
ctx.en: Her English is already excellent; add Spanish and she'll be even stronger on the job market.

ctx.s: 有了新的研发中心，这家公司{如虎添翼}，发展得更快了。
ctx.en: With its new research centre the company, already strong, is growing even faster.

ctx.s: “听说你们组又来了个高手？”“是啊，这下我们{如虎添翼}！”
ctx.en: "I hear another expert has joined your group?" "Yes, now we're unstoppable!"

ctx.s: 这位老将经验丰富，加上年轻助手的帮助，更是{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: The veteran has plenty of experience, and with a young assistant's help he is stronger than ever.

ctx.s: 对于一个优秀的厨师来说，一套好刀能让他{如虎添翼}。
ctx.en: For a skilled chef, a good set of knives makes him even better.

bad.s: 他从来没学过编程，买了新电脑真是{如虎添翼}。
bad.en: (meant: he has never learned to code, so the new computer is a big help)
bad.why: The tiger must already be strong; it cannot describe a beginner getting basic help.

bad.s: 路上本来就堵，又下起大雨，真是{如虎添翼}。
bad.en: (meant: the roads were jammed, and then heavy rain made it worse)
bad.why: It is praise for gaining strength; for one misfortune piling on another, use the 'snow on top of frost' idiom instead.

lit: like a fish that has found water

story.text: Liu Bei grew very close to Zhuge Liang, and his sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei were displeased. Liu Bei told them: having Kongming is to me like a fish having water, so I hope you will say no more about it. After that they let the matter drop.

use.how: A predicate, often 在……如鱼得水 or 过得如鱼得水. Said of a person who thrives in a place, job or company that suits them perfectly.

near.diff: 得心应手 is a skill or tool working smoothly in your hands; 如鱼得水 is a person thriving in an environment that suits them.

cue: A shy accountant who loved acting finally joins a theatre company, and there he thrives. How is he doing in his new world?

ctx.s: 他性格外向，做销售工作{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: He's outgoing, so he is in his element working in sales.

ctx.s: 搬到大城市以后，喜欢热闹的她过得{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: After moving to the big city, she, who loves bustle, is thriving.

ctx.s: 这位老师在新学校{如鱼得水}，学生们都很喜欢她。
ctx.en: The teacher is in her element at the new school, and the students all love her.

ctx.s: “你在国外习惯吗？”“刚开始不行，现在已经{如鱼得水}了。”
ctx.en: "Have you settled in abroad?" "Not at first, but now I'm completely at home."

ctx.s: 他在原来的公司处处受限，换了工作后反而{如鱼得水}。
ctx.en: He was held back at every turn at his old company, but in his new job he is flourishing.

ctx.s: 在自己擅长的领域里，他{如鱼得水}，很快就成了专家。
ctx.en: In the field he is good at, he was in his element and soon became an expert.

bad.s: 收到生日礼物，他高兴得{如鱼得水}。
bad.en: (meant: he was overjoyed to get a birthday present)
bad.why: It is not a burst of joy at a moment; it describes thriving in a setting or relationship that suits you.

bad.s: 他跑完步口渴极了，喝了一瓶水，{如鱼得水}。
bad.en: (meant: after the run he was thirsty and felt great after drinking water)
bad.why: The water is a figure for a fitting environment; it is never about the relief of drinking.

mean: to pull together to get through a crisis
lit: in the same boat, crossing the river together

story.text: In The Art of War, Sunzi observes that the people of Wu and the people of Yue hate each other. Yet if they are crossing a river in the same boat and a storm strikes, they will help one another like a person's left and right hands.

use.how: A predicate for several people facing one hardship: 大家要同舟共济，共渡难关。 Often an appeal to stick together.

near.diff: 齐心协力 is working together on any task; 同舟共济 stresses people sharing one danger or crisis and helping each other through it.

cue: A storm knocks out power across town, and neighbours share generators, food and medicine until it's over. What are they doing?

ctx.s: 公司遇到困难，老板希望大家{同舟共济}。
ctx.en: The company is in trouble, and the boss hopes everyone will pull together.

ctx.s: 停电那几天，邻居们{同舟共济}，互相送水送药。
ctx.en: During the days without power, the neighbours stuck together and brought each other water and medicine.

ctx.s: 夫妻之间，最重要的是在困难时{同舟共济}。
ctx.en: Between husband and wife, the most important thing is to stand together in hard times.

ctx.s: “这次洪水太严重了。”“是啊，只有{同舟共济}才能渡过难关。”
ctx.en: "This flood is terrible." "Yes, only by pulling together can we get through it."

ctx.s: 那年工厂差点倒闭，全体员工{同舟共济}，硬是撑了过来。
ctx.en: That year the factory nearly went under, but all the workers pulled together and somehow held on.

ctx.s: 球队连续输球，队长说这时候更要{同舟共济}，不能互相埋怨。
ctx.en: After a run of defeats, the captain said this was the time to stick together, not to blame each other.

bad.s: 周末我和朋友{同舟共济}，一起去吃火锅。
bad.en: (meant: at the weekend my friends and I went out for hotpot together)
bad.why: It needs a shared crisis to get through; it cannot mean simply doing something fun together.

bad.s: 他一个人{同舟共济}，熬过了最难的日子。
bad.en: (meant: on his own, he got through his hardest days)
bad.why: It describes several people in one plight helping each other; one person alone cannot do it.

mean: springing up everywhere like bamboo shoots
lit: bamboo shoots after a spring rain, all shooting up at once

use.how: Almost always 像/如雨后春笋般 + 出现/涌现/冒出来. Said of many new things of one kind appearing quickly.

near.diff: 层出不穷 is new ones coming one after another without end; 雨后春笋 is a sudden burst of many at once, like fast growth.

cue: Within two years, electric-scooter rental firms appeared on every corner of the city. How did they appear?

ctx.s: 这几年，奶茶店像{雨后春笋}一样开满了街头。
ctx.en: In the last few years, bubble-tea shops have sprung up all over the streets.

ctx.s: 网上购物流行以后，快递公司如{雨后春笋}般出现。
ctx.en: Once online shopping took off, delivery companies sprang up everywhere.

ctx.s: 城市周边，新的小区如{雨后春笋}般建了起来。
ctx.en: Around the city, new housing estates have been springing up one after another.

ctx.s: “现在怎么到处都是健身房？”“是啊，跟{雨后春笋}似的。”
ctx.en: "How come there are gyms everywhere now?" "I know, they're popping up like mushrooms."

ctx.s: 随着人工智能的发展，相关的创业公司如{雨后春笋}般冒了出来。
ctx.en: With the rise of artificial intelligence, start-ups in the field have mushroomed.

ctx.s: 那个年代，各种文学杂志如{雨后春笋}般涌现，年轻人争相投稿。
ctx.en: In those years literary magazines sprang up everywhere, and young people rushed to send in their writing.

bad.s: 他家门口如{雨后春笋}般开了一家咖啡店。
bad.en: (meant: a café opened right outside his home)
bad.why: It needs many things appearing at once; one new shop cannot spring up like bamboo shoots.

bad.s: 经济不好，小商店如{雨后春笋}般纷纷倒闭。
bad.en: (meant: with the economy bad, small shops closed one after another)
bad.why: Bamboo shoots shoot up; the image is of things appearing, never of them closing or disappearing.

lit: the smoke dissipates and the clouds scatter

use.how: A predicate, often with 一下子, 早已 or 都: 误会都烟消云散了。 Said of worries, anger, doubts or past glory vanishing without a trace.

near.diff: 一笔勾销 is deliberately cancelling a debt or grudge; 烟消云散 is a feeling or thing fading away of itself.

cue: You were furious with your friend, but after she explained and apologised, the anger simply dissolved. What happened to it?

ctx.s: 听到孩子平安的消息，她的担心一下子{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: When she heard her child was safe, her worry vanished at once.

ctx.s: 两人把话说开以后，之前的误会都{烟消云散}了。
ctx.en: Once the two of them talked it through, the earlier misunderstandings all melted away.

ctx.s: 考完最后一门，这一学期的压力全都{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: After the last exam, the whole term's stress just evaporated.

ctx.s: “你还生他的气吗？”“早就{烟消云散}了。”
ctx.en: "Are you still angry with him?" "That was gone long ago."

ctx.s: 曾经辉煌的王朝早已{烟消云散}，只留下几段古城墙。
ctx.en: The once-glorious dynasty has long since vanished, leaving only a few stretches of ancient wall.

ctx.s: 看到检查报告一切正常，他心里的疑虑才{烟消云散}。
ctx.en: Only when he saw that the test results were all normal did his doubts disappear.

bad.s: 我的钥匙{烟消云散}了，到处都找不到。
bad.en: (meant: my keys have vanished and I can't find them anywhere)
bad.why: It is for feelings, doubts or past glory fading away, not for an everyday object that has been lost.

bad.s: 他没说再见，就{烟消云散}地离开了。
bad.en: (meant: he left without a trace, not even saying goodbye)
bad.why: It describes feelings or glory fading, not a person walking off without a trace; it is not used as an adverb of leaving.

mean: right by every law of nature, beyond question
lit: the constant course of Heaven and the right order of Earth

story.text: In the Zuo Commentary, the statesman Zi Taishu repeats what Zichan once taught him: the rites are the constant course of Heaven, the right order of Earth, and the conduct of the people. From these words came the phrase for something self-evidently right.

use.how: A predicate, mostly ……是天经地义的（事）. Said of a duty or right so obvious that no one should question it.

near.diff: 理所当然 is simply 'only natural, as expected'; 天经地义 is stronger, a principle beyond all argument.

cue: Your boss asks why you expect pay for the extra hours you worked. To you it needs no argument at all. What is it?

ctx.s: 欠钱还钱，这是{天经地义}的事。
ctx.en: If you owe money, you pay it back; that's simply how it is.

ctx.s: 在很多人看来，父母照顾孩子是{天经地义}的。
ctx.en: To many people, parents looking after their children goes without saying.

ctx.s: “加班凭什么不给钱？”“对，干活拿工资，{天经地义}！”
ctx.en: "Why should overtime be unpaid?" "Exactly. You work, you get paid. It's beyond question!"

ctx.s: 治病救人是医生{天经地义}的职责，不能看病人有没有钱。
ctx.en: Healing the sick is a doctor's unquestionable duty, whether or not the patient has money.

ctx.s: 古人认为尊敬长辈{天经地义}，不需要任何理由。
ctx.en: People in ancient times held that respecting one's elders was self-evidently right and needed no reason.

ctx.s: 顾客付了钱，要求商品质量合格，本来就{天经地义}。
ctx.en: A customer who has paid has every right to expect goods of proper quality.

bad.s: 他从小就{天经地义}地很聪明。
bad.en: (meant: he has been naturally clever since childhood)
bad.why: It is about what is morally right or just, not about innate talent or what someone is like by nature.

bad.s: 这次考试的题目很{天经地义}，大家都会做。
bad.en: (meant: the exam questions were straightforward and everyone could do them)
bad.why: It judges a duty or right as beyond question; it cannot mean simple, easy or obvious.

mean: seamless, with no trace of flaws (a plan, a cover-up)
lit: the clothes of heaven have no seams

story.text: On a summer night a man named Guo Han was lying in his courtyard when a woman came floating down from the sky: the Weaver Girl. He noticed that her clothes had no seams at all. When he asked why, she told him that heavenly clothes are not made with needle and thread.

use.how: A predicate or a complement after 得: 计划天衣无缝, 配合得天衣无缝. Said of plans, teamwork, lies or work so well made that no flaw shows.

near.diff: 完美无缺 is anything perfect; 天衣无缝 stresses that no gap or trace shows, so it suits plans, teamwork and cover stories.

cue: At the surprise party the guests hid, the cake came on time, and the birthday girl suspected nothing at all. How was it all carried out?

ctx.s: 两位舞者配合得{天衣无缝}，观众掌声不断。
ctx.en: The two dancers moved together flawlessly, and the audience kept applauding.

ctx.s: 他以为自己的谎话{天衣无缝}，结果还是被妈妈识破了。
ctx.en: He thought his lie was airtight, but his mother saw through it anyway.

ctx.s: 这部推理小说的情节设计得{天衣无缝}，直到最后才揭晓凶手。
ctx.en: The plot of this mystery novel is seamless, and the killer is revealed only at the very end.

ctx.s: “你的计划真的没问题吗？”“放心，{天衣无缝}！”
ctx.en: "Are you sure your plan has no holes?" "Don't worry, it's watertight!"

ctx.s: 小偷自以为作案{天衣无缝}，却被监控拍得清清楚楚。
ctx.en: The thief thought he had left no trace, but the security camera caught everything clearly.

ctx.s: 修复后的古画和原作衔接得{天衣无缝}，看不出任何痕迹。
ctx.en: The restored parts of the old painting blend seamlessly with the original, without a visible trace.

bad.s: 这个杯子{天衣无缝}，怎么摔都摔不坏。
bad.en: (meant: this cup is unbreakable however you drop it)
bad.why: It means no flaw or gap shows in how something is put together, not that an object is strong or durable.

bad.s: 她长得{天衣无缝}，像明星一样漂亮。
bad.en: (meant: she is flawlessly beautiful, like a film star)
bad.why: It describes plans, teamwork or craftsmanship that show no flaw, never a person's natural looks or beauty.

mean: the truth finally comes to light
lit: the water level falls and the rocks emerge

story.text: In his Second Ode on the Red Cliff, Su Shi describes going back to the cliff in early winter: the mountains high, the moon small, the water low and the rocks standing out of it. The image of rocks revealed as the water falls later came to mean a hidden truth coming to light.

use.how: Often 查个水落石出 or 事情终于水落石出了. Said of an affair or mystery whose truth becomes fully clear, usually after investigation.

near.diff: 真相大白 simply states that the truth is now known; 水落石出 stresses it coming out after digging, and fits 查个水落石出.

cue: Someone keeps taking food from the office fridge. You vow to keep digging until you know exactly who it is. What will you do?

ctx.s: 钱包到底是谁拿的，老师说一定要查个{水落石出}。
ctx.en: The teacher said she would get to the bottom of who took the wallet.

ctx.s: 经过警方三个月的调查，这起案件终于{水落石出}。
ctx.en: After three months of police investigation, the truth of the case finally came out.

ctx.s: “你相信他是清白的吗？”“等事情{水落石出}，大家就知道了。”
ctx.en: "Do you believe he's innocent?" "When the truth comes out, everyone will know."

ctx.s: 这件事不弄个{水落石出}，我睡不着觉。
ctx.en: I won't be able to sleep until I get to the bottom of this.

ctx.s: 记者追查了好几年，那桩丑闻才终于{水落石出}。
ctx.en: Only after journalists dug into it for several years did the truth of the scandal finally come out.

ctx.s: 时间会证明一切，真相总有{水落石出}的一天。
ctx.en: Time will tell; one day the truth will come to light.

bad.s: 我晚饭想吃什么，到现在还没{水落石出}。
bad.en: (meant: I still haven't decided what to have for dinner)
bad.why: It is about a hidden truth being uncovered, not about making up one's mind.

bad.s: 他是一个{水落石出}的人，从来不说谎。
bad.en: (meant: he is an open, honest person who never lies)
bad.why: It describes a hidden matter becoming clear, never a person's character or honesty.
